note: Source: De Lacy O'Leary, The Daily Office and Theotokia of the Coptic Church (London, 1911), pp. 117-130, public domain. First day of the weekly Theotokia hymn cycle (Phase 2 of the Coptic Agpeya rebuild, following completion of all seven hours and the Midnight Office). Structure: a Psali ('Our Lord Jesus'), an Alternative (Marian) Psali, then the Theotokia proper -- eight sections, most paired with a paraphrase and a Gospel lection (Luke 1 and 2, the Annunciation/Visitation/Benedictus/Nunc Dimittis cycle), a Conclusion, and a seasonal Hymn on the Resurrection (Easter to the end of Hatur only -- included as its own labeled component since this app does not yet have seasonal on/off logic for Theotokia additions). O'Leary's book also contains extensive 'additional matter' for this day -- secondary and tertiary paraphrases from other manuscript traditions (Types II, III, IV), scholarly variants aimed at textual critics -- deliberately not built here; this office follows only O'Leary's Section A, 'the Coptic text common to all types', which is what an ordinary devotional user would actually pray. IMPORTANT SOURCING NOTE: this content came from this app's automated Google Drive text-extraction tool rather than transcribed directly from page images. This is the same underlying book and scan as the seven hours (Josh split it into two PDF files, not two different sources) -- the difference is page layout, not scan quality: the Theotokia's pages interleave multiple manuscript-witness columns (Text A, Text Q, Text K), marginal folio references, and footnotes inline with the main text, which is far harder for automated linearization to get right than the hours' simple continuous-prose pages. Every component here is flagged in its own meta as a lower-confidence tier pending a human read-through against the actual page images, same as any other book in this project awaiting verification before GREEN.

Source: De Lacy O'Leary, The Daily Office and Theotokia of the Coptic Church (London, 1911), pp. 148-155, public domain. Second day of the weekly Theotokia hymn cycle. As with Sunday, O'Leary's extensive scholarly 'additional matter' for this day (manuscript-variant paraphrases) is deliberately not built here -- out of scope for a devotional app.
